misconceptions.statement: The pupil identifies a shape by a familiar orientation or appearance instead of its defining properties.
The pupil treats shape categories as mutually exclusive and does not recognise that a square can also be a rectangle and a parallelogram.
The pupil confuses faces, edges and vertices or counts features from a drawing without considering hidden parts of the solid.
The pupil thinks parallel lines must be horizontal or perpendicular lines must be vertical/horizontal rather than reasoning from the relationship between the lines.
The pupil confuses radius and diameter or does not recognise that every diameter passes through the centre and equals two radii.
The pupil classifies an angle from the orientation of its arms rather than the amount of turn/opening.
The pupil accepts a line as a line of symmetry when corresponding points would not reflect to matching positions across it.
The pupil rotates or reflects a shape while translating it, instead of moving every point the same distance in the same direction.
The pupil describes a rotation only as 'turning' and does not attend to the centre, direction and angle of rotation.
